span.label: null-result
span.quote: We conclude that repetition suppression accompanies repetition priming but is unlikely to be its cause.

span.label: repetition suppression in inferotemporal cortex
span.quote: Repetition suppression is a physiological phenomenon, first demonstrated in recording studies of monkey inferotemporal cortex (IT), whereby the strength of the neuronal response to a visual stimulus declines over successive presentations.

span.label: electrophysiology
span.quote: We monitored the activity of 152 neurons in anterior IT (85 in m1; 67 in m2) during the same 118 sessions on which the behavioral analysis was based.

span.label: The correlation analysis had limited power, so a very weak cross-trial correlation between suppression and priming cannot be excluded.
span.quote: Because the correlation analysis was of limited power, we cannot rule out the possibility that there was a very weak cross-trial correlation between suppression and priming.

span.label: Independent noise in firing rates and reaction times could in principle have masked an underlying weak correlation.
span.quote: We cannot absolutely rule out the possibility that the firing rates and reaction times were subject to large independent sources of noise that masked an underlying weak correlation between suppression and priming.

span.label: The design confounds elapsed time with the number of intervening trials, so the effect of time interval per se was not tested.
span.quote: The experiment was not designed to test explicitly the impact of time interval, as distinct from the number of intervening trials, between repetitions.

span.label: The standard Gaussian tuning-curve method for assessing selectivity change could not be applied to IT neurons, forcing an alternative rank-based analysis.
span.quote: This approach is not feasible for IT neurons because IT tuning profiles are not generally well fit by Gaussian functions, nor are the dimensions of feature selectivity necessarily manipulable parametrically.

span.label: replicates → Li et al. 1993; Ringo 1996 (late onset of repetition suppression in IT)
span.quote: In agreement with previous reports obtained outside the context of the priming paradigm (Li et al. 1993; Ringo 1996), we found that the initial phase of the visual response was identical between the first and second presentations and that suppression took hold only late in the response (Fig. 6).

span.label: replicates → Maccotta and Buckner 2004; Sayres and Grill-Spector 2006; Wig et al. 2005 (no priming-BOLD correlation in ventral stream)
span.quote: This result is consistent with the findings of several recent studies that failed to detect any correlation across human subjects between priming of behavior and BOLD signal reduction in regions of ventral stream visual cortex (Maccotta and Buckner 2004; Sayres and Grill-Spector 2006; Wig et al. 2005).

span.label: contradicts → the sharpening model of repetition suppression (Desimone 1996; Wiggs and Martin 1998)
span.quote: They clearly conform more closely to the predictions of the scaling model (Fig. 9B) than to those of the sharpening model (Fig. 9A).

span.label: builds-on → Maljkovic and Nakayama (1994) memory kernel analysis
span.quote: To determine whether the priming effects we observed could be partially attributable to response repetition, we adapted from Maljkovic and Nakayama (1994) the method of memory kernel analysis (see METHODS, Memory kernel analysis of response repetition effects).

span.label: correlation
span.quote: and suppression To assess whether neuronal suppression and behavioral priming were correlated, we performed a Pearson correlation analysis across all pairs of trials between measures of both priming and repetition suppression.
